questions.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
questions.description:
Read a single line containing a string of **lowercase English letters** (length ≥ 1 — the line is never empty). Print the **longest contiguous substring** of that line which reads the same forwards and backwards (a palindrome).

If more than one substring of the maximum length is a palindrome, print the one that **starts earliest** in the string. Every single character is itself a palindrome of length 1, so an answer always exists, even when no longer palindrome does.

### Input
A single line of lowercase letters, e.g.
```
babad
```

### Output
The longest palindromic substring, e.g.
```
bab
```

### Worked examples

**Odd-length palindrome**
```
Input:  babad
Output: bab
```
`bab` and `aba` are both palindromes of length 3; `bab` starts first (at index 0), so it is printed instead of `aba`.

**Even-length palindrome**
```
Input:  cbbd
Output: bb
```
`bb` (indices 1-2) is the longest palindrome here — there is no odd-length palindrome longer than a single character, so the answer is even-length. Watch out for this case: a palindrome can be centred **between** two letters, not just on one.

### Tie-break rule
When two or more substrings share the maximum length, print whichever one **begins first** in the input string, regardless of where the others occur.

starterCode.python:
import sys


def main():
    s = sys.stdin.readline().strip()

    # TODO: find the longest contiguous palindromic substring of s.
    # If multiple substrings tie for the longest length, print the one
    # that starts earliest in s. Remember a palindrome can be centred
    # on a single letter (odd length) or between two letters (even length).


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

no palindrome longer than one character
the whole string is a palindrome
tie between two equal-length palindromes, earliest start wins
whole string is a short even-length palindrome
